gap: No result ChatGPT got states what named testers measured side by side: every tested 25,000 mAh bank delivered about 74-78 Wh of its roughly 90 Wh label and none held 100 W to empty, while Macworld's two-cycle MacBook Pro score spread from 92% (Anker 25K 165W) to 128% (Sharge HyperTower 170).
standout_why: Compared against dupple.com (cited; says "Compared from vendor specs and store pages, not tested hands-on"; its only usable-energy figure is an unattributed "~63-70 Wh" for the Anker), powerbanks.fyi under-$100 and 25,000mAh pages (maker-listed mAh, Wh, weight and price only), and the us.ugreen.com and iniushop.com store listings (marketing specs and prices). None gives a measured delivered-Wh figure, a sustained-100 W result or a Macworld Test Score. Not compared: the TechRadar AU article body came back truncated, and the Best Buy, techwithall and knowledgelib pages were not opened.
decides: It confirms the pick more than it changes it. Measured delivered energy is within about 4 Wh across the UGREEN 145W, INIU P63, Anker 25K, Sharge HyperTower 170 and Baseus FC41 25K, so capacity does not separate them and price and port wattage still decide; the UGREEN 145W at $59.98 stays the value pick. Caveat for that pick: the only bench test found (techtest.org, June 2023) used an earlier 100 W unit without PPS, while UGREEN's US page today lists 28 V/5 A 140 W and PPS, which explains why reviews disagree. It does change the convenience slot: the Anker 25K 165W that ChatGPT showed at $91.19 scored lowest in Macworld's test (92%), and the Sharge HyperTower 170, also with two built-in cables, scored highest (128%) at $75.90 on sharge.com today. For our Baseus FC41 25K, the one bench test found says 140 W is brief and sustained output is about 55-65 W, so it should not be sold as a 140 W laptop bank on measured evidence.
